text:
Question: The nurse in the telemetry unit is caring for a 60-year-old client who has a history of several episodes of ventricular tachycardia in the past 48 hours. A normal QT interval was observed earlier today. A left ventricular assist device was inserted 2 weeks ago.
Electrocardiogram:
[image.png](https://classroom.galencollege.edu/courses/8273805/files/359448245/preview)
Select the best option to complete the following sentence.
The nurse should first ___________.
A. check the client’s deep tendon reflexes
B. asses (collect data about/lpn) the client’s Chvostek and Trousseau signs
C. hold the client’s next dose of amiodarone
D. administer magnesium sulfate, 2 g, IV over 2 minutes for the client
Correct answer: D. administer magnesium sulfate, 2 g, IV over 2 minutes for the client
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• administer magnesium sulfate, 2 g, IV over 2 minutes for the client
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “administer magnesium sulfate, 2 g, IV over 2 minutes for the client” – Source identifies torsades; magnesium treats it
Not correct:
• “check the client’s deep tendon reflexes” – Reflex assessment delays rhythm treatment
• “asses (collect data about/lpn) the client’s Chvostek and Trousseau signs” – Calcium signs are secondary
• “hold the client’s next dose of amiodarone” – Holding a later dose does not treat current rhythm
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a patient who is receiving a high dose of intravenous az
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a patient who is receiving a high dose of intravenous azithromycin to treat an infection. The patient is also taking acetaminophen for pain. The nurse should expect to review which lab values when monitoring for this drug’s side effects?
A. Electrolytes
B. Liver enzymes
C. Complete blood counts
D. Urinalysis
Correct answer: B. Liver enzymes
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Liver enzymes
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Liver enzymes” – Both agents can injure liver
Not correct:
• “Electrolytes” – Not the main shared toxicity
• “Complete blood counts” – Not primary monitoring for hepatic injury
• “Urinalysis” – Does not detect liver toxicity directly
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: The nurse provides home-care instructions for a patient who will take a high dos
text: Question: The nurse provides home-care instructions for a patient who will take a high dose of azithromycin after discharge from the hospital. Which statement by the patient indicates an understanding of the teaching?
A. “I should avoid dairy products while taking this drug.”
B. “I should expect diarrhea to be a common, mild side effect.”
C. “I may take antacids 2 hours before taking this drug.”
D. “I should take acetaminophen for fever or mild pain.”
Correct answer: C. “I may take antacids 2 hours before taking this drug.”
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• “I may take antacids 2 hours before taking this drug.”
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• ““I may take antacids 2 hours before taking this drug.”” – Separating relevant antacids avoids absorption interaction
Not correct:
• ““I should avoid dairy products while taking this drug.”” – Dairy avoidance is not routinely required
• ““I should expect diarrhea to be a common, mild side effect.”” – Diarrhea can occur, but significant or persistent diarrhea needs evaluation
• ““I should take acetaminophen for fever or mild pain.”” – Additional acetaminophen may increase hepatic risk
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

text: Question: A nurse is conducting a physical assessment of a 90-year-old client. The nurse understands that special considerations when working with older adults include which of the following?
A. Older adults do not require a “head to toe assessment,” so an abbreviated assessment should be done.
B. The nurse needs to leave the assessment that is most painful until the end.
C. It is important to complete the entire physical assessment at one time, conducting a “head to toe assessment.”
D. The nurse needs to first direct the assessment to that which is most likely associated with the presenting problem.
Correct answer: D. The nurse needs to first direct the assessment to that which is most likely associated with the presenting problem.
Topic: Health Promotion & Prevention
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• The nurse needs to first direct the assessment to that which is most likely associated with the presenting problem.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The nurse needs to first direct the assessment to that which is most likely associated …” – Prioritize presenting problem
Not correct:
• “Older adults do not require a “head to toe assessment,” so an abbreviated assessment sh…” – Older adults still need comprehensive assessment
• “The nurse needs to leave the assessment that is most painful until the end.” – Painful assessment need not invariably be last
• “It is important to complete the entire physical assessment at one time, conducting a “h…” – Fatigue may require breaks

text: Question: Using the Resident Assessment Instrument (RAI), the nurse identifies a trigger for a male nursing home resident who requires an indwelling urinary catheter from the Minimum Data Set (MDS). Which should the nurse do next?
A. Refer to the appropriate quality measures.
B. Assign suitable nursing interventions.
C. Institute agency-approved catheter care.
D. Develop an individualized care plan.
Correct answer: A. Refer to the appropriate quality measures.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Refer to the appropriate quality measures.

• “Refer to the appropriate quality measures.” – Investigate identified trigger before planning
Not correct:

slides.title: A nurse hears a colleague tell a nursing student that they never touch a patient
text: Question: A nurse hears a colleague tell a nursing student that they never touch a patient unless they are performing a procedure or doing an assessment. From a caring perspective, the nurse tells the student
A. touch is only used when a patient is in pain.
B. touch forms a connection between nurse and patient.
C. touch is a type of verbal communication.
D. they do not touch the patients either.
Correct answer: B. touch forms a connection between nurse and patient.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• touch forms a connection between nurse and patient.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “touch forms a connection between nurse and patient.” – Appropriate touch strengthens connection
Not correct:
• “touch is only used when a patient is in pain.” – Comforting touch is not limited to pain
• “touch is a type of verbal communication.” – Touch is nonverbal
• “they do not touch the patients either.” – Reinforces an unnecessarily restrictive approach

slides.title: Which of the following statements are true about long-term care? (Select all tha
text: Question: Which of the following statements are true about long-term care? (Select all that apply.)
A. Most long-term care is paid for by Medicare.
B. The number of older adults needing long-term care services is expected to increase 233%.
C. Costs of long-term care have outpaced inflation since 2003.
D. Long-term care is the most cost-effective manner in which to care for older adults.
E. Most individuals in the United States have purchased long-term care insurance.
Correct answers: B. The number of older adults needing long-term care services is expected to increase 233%.; C. Costs of long-term care have outpaced inflation since 2003.
Topic: Health Promotion & Prevention
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• The number of older adults needing long-term care services is expected to increase 233%.
• Costs of long-term care have outpaced inflation since 2003.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The number of older adults needing long-term care services is expected to increase 233%.” – Source projects increased need
• “Costs of long-term care have outpaced inflation since 2003.” – Source reports historical cost growth
Not correct:
• “Most long-term care is paid for by Medicare.” – Medicare generally does not cover custodial long-term care
• “Long-term care is the most cost-effective manner in which to care for older adults.” – Cost-effectiveness depends on setting and need
• “Most individuals in the United States have purchased long-term care insurance.” – Most people lack dedicated long-term care insurance
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

text: Question: The nurse is concerned that a break in sterile procedure has occured.  Which of the following actions would caused a break in sterile field?
A. Grasping the edge of the outermost flap and opening it away from oneself
B. Keeping objects on the field 1 inch from the edge
C. Keeping the sterile field in eyesight
D. Transferring a sterile object to a sterile field with a clean gloved hand
Correct answer: D. Transferring a sterile object to a sterile field with a clean gloved hand
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Transferring a sterile object to a sterile field with a clean gloved hand
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Transferring a sterile object to a sterile field with a clean gloved hand” – Clean gloves contaminate sterile objects
Not correct:
• “Grasping the edge of the outermost flap and opening it away from oneself” – Opening away avoids reaching over field
• “Keeping objects on the field 1 inch from the edge” – Keep items outside the contaminated border
• “Keeping the sterile field in eyesight” – Visibility preserves monitoring
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 1 - Safety & Infection Prevention & Control, slide 5: “You MUST use sterile gloves, instruments, devices and  mask”
Your slide says sterile technique needs sterile gloves, which supports the answer; the exact clean-glove wording is not on your slides.

slides.title: A nurse is performing a sterile dressing change for a client. Which of the follo
text: Question: A nurse is performing a sterile dressing change for a client.  Which of the following actions by the nurse would compromise the sterility of the procedure? (Select all that apply.)
A. The nurse leans across the sterile field.
B. The nurse turning their back on the sterile field.
C. Opening a sterile package and then dropping the item onto a non-sterile field.
D. The nurse opens a sterile package and drops a sterile item in the one inch border around the field.

Correct answers: A. The nurse leans across the sterile field.; B. The nurse turning their back on the sterile field.; C. Opening a sterile package and then dropping the item onto a non-sterile field.; D. The nurse opens a sterile package and drops a sterile item in the one inch border around the field.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• The nurse leans across the sterile field.
• The nurse turning their back on the sterile field.
• Opening a sterile package and then dropping the item onto a non-sterile field.
• The nurse opens a sterile package and drops a sterile item in the one inch border around the field.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The nurse leans across the sterile field.” – Reaching over field risks contamination
• “The nurse turning their back on the sterile field.” – Unobserved field is considered contaminated
• “Opening a sterile package and then dropping the item onto a non-sterile field.” – Nonsterile surface contaminates item
• “The nurse opens a sterile package and drops a sterile item in the one inch border aroun…” – Outer inch is contaminated
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: A patient who takes a diuretic and a b-blocker to control blood pressure is sche
text: Question: A patient who takes a diuretic and a b-blocker to control blood pressure is scheduled for breast reconstruction surgery. Which patient information is most important to communicate to the health care provider before surgery?
A. Hematocrit 36%
B. Pulse rate 58 beats/minute
C. Blood pressure 144/82
D. Serum potassium 3.2 mEq/L
Correct answer: D. Serum potassium 3.2 mEq/L
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Serum potassium 3.2 mEq/L
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Serum potassium 3.2 mEq/L” – Low potassium raises perioperative arrhythmia risk
Not correct:
• “Hematocrit 36%” – Mildly low or near-normal value
• “Pulse rate 58 beats/minute” – Beta blockers may explain mild bradycardia
• “Blood pressure 144/82” – Mild elevation is less urgent
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 8 - Cardiac, slide 7: “Hypokalemia”
Thiazide diuretics cause hypokalemia; the surgical-risk reasoning itself is not in your materials.

text: Question: A client with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) is scheduled for hemodialysis in one hour.  The nurse should notify the primary health care provider that the client has a
A. Sodium 145 mEq/L
B. Creatinine 3.5 mg/dl
C. Potassium 6.8 mEq/L
D. BUN of 60 mg/dl
Correct answer: C. Potassium 6.8 mEq/L
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Potassium 6.8 mEq/L
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Potassium 6.8 mEq/L” – Severe hyperkalemia threatens cardiac rhythm
Not correct:
• “Sodium 145 mEq/L” – At upper end of normal
• “Creatinine 3.5 mg/dl” – Expected elevation in ESRD
• “BUN of 60 mg/dl” – Expected elevation in ESRD
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 7 - Renal, slide 7: “Hyperkalemia”
The slide lists hyperkalemia for acute kidney injury; ESRD-specific lab values are not covered.

slides.title: As the nurse you are providing care for a client who is 2 days post-op and has s
text: Question: As the nurse you are providing care for a client who is 2 days post-op and has still not had a bowel movement nor have they passed flatus.  On assessment, you note the abdomen is distended and no bowel sounds are noted in the four quadrants. You notify the MD. What non-invasive nursing interventions can you perform without a MD order?
A. Encourage at least 3000 mL of fluids per day
B. Encourage ambulation, maintain NPO status, and monitor intake and output
C. Administer IV fluids
D. Insert a nasogastric attached to intermittent suction
Correct answer: B. Encourage ambulation, maintain NPO status, and monitor intake and output
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Encourage ambulation, maintain NPO status, and monitor intake and output
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Encourage ambulation, maintain NPO status, and monitor intake and output” – NPO, mobility and I&O are supportive measures
Not correct:
• “Encourage at least 3000 mL of fluids per day” – Oral fluids inappropriate with suspected ileus
• “Administer IV fluids” – IV fluids require an order
• “Insert a nasogastric attached to intermittent suction” – NG decompression requires an order
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: A nurse is developing a care plan for a patient who is at risk for developing pn
text: Question: A nurse is developing a care plan for a patient who is at risk for developing pneumonia after surgery. Which of the following are appropriate nursing interventions? (Select all that apply.)
A. Encourage early ambulation and patient to eat meals in beside chair
B. Encourage patient intake of 3000 ml/day of fluids if not contraindicated
C. Encourage patient to use the incentive spirometer device 10 times every 1-2 hours while awake
D. Repositioning every 3-4 hours

Correct answers: A. Encourage early ambulation and patient to eat meals in beside chair; B. Encourage patient intake of 3000 ml/day of fluids if not contraindicated; C. Encourage patient to use the incentive spirometer device 10 times every 1-2 hours while awake
Topic: Respiratory
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• Encourage early ambulation and patient to eat meals in beside chair
• Encourage patient intake of 3000 ml/day of fluids if not contraindicated
• Encourage patient to use the incentive spirometer device 10 times every 1-2 hours while awake
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Encourage early ambulation and patient to eat meals in beside chair” – Mobilization improves ventilation
• “Encourage patient intake of 3000 ml/day of fluids if not contraindicated” – Hydration helps clear secretions if allowed
• “Encourage patient to use the incentive spirometer device 10 times every 1-2 hours while…” – Incentive spirometry encourages lung expansion
Not correct:
• “Repositioning every 3-4 hours” – Reposition more frequently as appropriate
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 6 - Respiratory, slide 4: “Increase fluids 2500-3000 ml/day”
• Unit 6 - Respiratory, slide 4: “Encourage client to turn, cough, and deep breath, splint chest wall, use incentive spirometer”

A. High oxygen flow rate
B. A humidifier
C. A nasal cannula
D. A Venturi mask
Correct answer: B. A humidifier

slides.title: Which of the following nursing diagnosis would the nurse expect to assign for a
text: Question: Which of the following nursing diagnosis would the nurse expect to assign for a client with diabetes insipidus ?
A. excess fluid volume related to intake greater than output.
B. risk for impaired skin integrity related to generalized edema.
C. sleep pattern disturbance related to frequent waking to void.
D. impaired gas exchange related to fluid retention in lungs.
Correct answer: C. sleep pattern disturbance related to frequent waking to void.
Topic: Endocrine & Metabolic
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• sleep pattern disturbance related to frequent waking to void.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “sleep pattern disturbance related to frequent waking to void.” – Nocturia interrupts sleep
Not correct:
• “excess fluid volume related to intake greater than output.” – DI causes water loss, not retention
• “risk for impaired skin integrity related to generalized edema.” – Generalized edema is not typical
• “impaired gas exchange related to fluid retention in lungs.” – Pulmonary fluid retention is not characteristic
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 9 - Endocrine, slide 6: “Polyuria, polydipsia, weakness,    anorectic, loses weight”
